Legal Standards.name: Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) — Water Code, Part 2.74 (commencing § 10720)
Legal Standards.note: SGMA is the primary statewide legal regime that directly regulates long-term groundwater storage outcomes by requiring basins to avoid 'undesirable results,' including 'reduction of groundwater storage' and 'chronic lowering of groundwater levels'.

key_elements.name: Sustainable groundwater management (definition)
key_elements.note: "Sustainable groundwater management" means the management and use of groundwater... without causing undesirable results.

key_elements.name: Undesirable result (definition)
key_elements.note: "Undesirable result" means... (1) Chronic lowering of groundwater levels... (2) Significant and unreasonable reduction of groundwater storage...

key_elements.name: Sustainable yield (definition)
key_elements.note: "Sustainable yield" means the maximum quantity... that can be withdrawn annually... without causing an undesirable result.

Legal Standards.name: SGMA Groundwater Sustainability Plan (GSP) Regulations — Title 23, CCR (DWR)
Legal Standards.note: The regulations operationalize 'storage' through minimum thresholds, measurable objectives, and required justification/monitoring—often using groundwater levels as a proxy for storage in practice.

key_elements.name: Minimum thresholds for chronic lowering
key_elements.note: "Minimum thresholds... shall be defined as follows... (1) Chronic Lowering... supported by... (A) The rate of groundwater elevation decline..."

key_elements.name: Minimum thresholds for reduction of groundwater storage
key_elements.note: "(2) Reduction of Groundwater Storage. The minimum threshold... shall be a total volume of groundwater that can be withdrawn... without... undesirable results."

key_elements.name: Measurable objectives and interim milestones
key_elements.note: "Each Agency shall establish measurable objectives, including interim milestones... to achieve the sustainability goal... within 20 years..."

Legal Standards.name: DWR Review/Evaluation Standard for GSPs — Water Code § 10733.4
Legal Standards.note: DWR formally evaluates whether a basin's plan and implementation is likely to achieve sustainability—meaning trends and storage outcomes are indirectly regulated via plan adequacy determinations.

key_elements.name: Plan evaluation and corrective actions
key_elements.note: "The department shall evaluate the groundwater sustainability plan... and issue an assessment... [with] recommended corrective actions..."

key_elements.name: DWR public description of evaluation
key_elements.note: "DWR evaluates GSPs to determine if they comply with SGMA... and whether implementation... is likely to achieve the sustainability goal..."

Legal Standards.name: State Intervention / Probationary Basin Standard — Water Code § 10735.2 (State Water Board)
Legal Standards.note: If plans are missing, inadequate, uncoordinated, or not implemented to achieve sustainability, the State Water Board can designate a basin probationary and impose interim requirements.

key_elements.name: Probationary basin authority
key_elements.note: "The board... may designate... as a probationary basin..."

key_elements.name: Practical triggering condition (SWRCB factsheet)
key_elements.note: "DWR... fails a plan or determines a plan is not being implemented in a manner likely to achieve sustainability..."

Legal Standards.name: Groundwater Basin Boundaries — DWR Bulletin 118
Legal Standards.note: DWR's authoritative basin framework defining management geography; frequently used to scope storage accounting and models.

key_elements.name: Bulletin 118 basin identification
key_elements.note: Bulletin 118 "identified... groundwater basins and subbasins... [including] storage capacity..."

Legal Standards.name: Well Construction Standards & Local Permitting — Water Code §§ 13800 et seq.
Legal Standards.note: California regulates well construction/abandonment through state-recommended standards and county/local enforcement by Local Enforcing Agencies (LEAs).

key_elements.name: Local enforcing agency role
key_elements.note: "A local enforcing agency (LEA), such as a county environmental health department, is tasked with... well permitting..."

Legal Standards.name: Porter–Cologne Water Quality Control Act — Water Code Division 7
Legal Standards.note: Storage interacts with managed aquifer recharge and groundwater quality; Regional Water Boards can require permits/conditions for discharges affecting groundwater quality.

Legal Standards.name: Groundwater Adjudications
Legal Standards.note: In adjudicated basins, storage/levels constrained through court-approved pumping limits; SGMA links to adjudication processes and 'undesirable results' concepts.

Tier 1.policy_name: Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) — Water Code, Part 2.74 (commencing § 10720)
Tier 1.note: Meets SGMA intent and is consistent with avoiding storage-related undesirable results. SGMA sustainability concept: management that can be maintained "without causing undesirable results." Avoidance of the undesirable results most directly connected to your metric: "Chronic lowering of groundwater levels..." and "reduction of groundwater storage..." (i.e., your trend is non-declining).

Tier 1.policy_name: SGMA Groundwater Sustainability Plan (GSP) Regulations — Title 23, CCR (DWR)
Tier 1.note: GSP regs still require minimum thresholds/measurable objectives and monitoring, even when trends are good: Minimum thresholds must be defined for storage and levels. Measurable objectives + interim milestones must exist.

Tier 2.policy_name: Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) — Water Code, Part 2.74 (commencing § 10720)
Tier 2.note: Not automatically a violation. SGMA does not require being above a "reference scenario"; it requires avoiding "significant and unreasonable" storage reduction and meeting locally adopted thresholds/objectives.

Tier 2.policy_name: Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) — Water Code, Part 2.74 (commencing § 10720)
Tier 2.note: The SGMA "undesirable result" definition explicitly includes "Significant and unreasonable reduction of groundwater storage." Your tier condition ("less than reference") flags a risk screen that the basin may be closer to that line, depending on how the GSA defined "significant/unreasonable."

Tier 2.policy_name: SGMA Groundwater Sustainability Plan (GSP) Regulations — Title 23, CCR (DWR)
Tier 2.note: GSP regulation requires a storage minimum threshold definition: "Minimum threshold... for reduction of groundwater storage shall be a total volume... withdrawable... without... undesirable results."

Tier 2.policy_name: Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) — Water Code, Part 2.74 (commencing § 10720)
Tier 2.relationship: Potentially met / potentially violated (depends on the GSP)
Tier 2.note: Met if modeled/observed storage remains above the GSP's minimum threshold(s) and on track with interim milestones. Violated/triggered only if "below reference" also corresponds to (or causes) exceedance of locally adopted minimum thresholds or failure to stay on the "reasonable path" to sustainability.

Tier 3.policy_name: Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) — Water Code, Part 2.74 (commencing § 10720)
Tier 3.note: Strongly implicated under SGMA; may indicate the basin is moving toward (or already in) chronic lowering and/or storage reduction conditions that must be prevented from becoming "significant and unreasonable." Statutory undesirable result includes "Chronic lowering of groundwater levels..." if it indicates significant/unreasonable depletion over the planning horizon.

Tier 3.policy_name: SGMA Groundwater Sustainability Plan (GSP) Regulations — Title 23, CCR (DWR)
Tier 3.note: GSP minimum thresholds for chronic lowering must be supported by "the rate of groundwater elevation decline" (your slope metric directly aligns with this regulatory concept). If interim milestones aren't being met, the plan may be found deficient in implementation: "measurable objectives, including interim milestones..."

Tier 3.policy_name: Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) — Water Code, Part 2.74 (commencing § 10720)
Tier 3.relationship: Potential violations (tier alone doesn't prove them, but it's the direction that matters)
Tier 3.note: If this declining trend causes exceedance of minimum thresholds (levels or storage), the basin is in/near an SGMA "undesirable result" condition.

Tier 3.policy_name: DWR Review/Evaluation Standard for GSPs — Water Code § 10733.4
Tier 3.note: Persistent decline inconsistent with the GSP's "reasonable path" can contribute to DWR concerns about whether implementation is likely to achieve sustainability.

Tier 4.policy_name: Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) — Water Code, Part 2.74 (commencing § 10720)
Tier 4.note: Highest likelihood of SGMA noncompliance in practice (because severe declines commonly push groundwater elevations/storage below local minimum thresholds and harm other SGMA indicators like subsidence and interconnected surface water).

Tier 4.policy_name: Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) — Water Code, Part 2.74 (commencing § 10720)
Tier 4.relationship: Likely violated / triggered (depending on adopted thresholds)
Tier 4.note: "Undesirable result" includes: "Chronic lowering of groundwater levels..." "Significant and unreasonable reduction of groundwater storage."

Tier 4.policy_name: SGMA Groundwater Sustainability Plan (GSP) Regulations — Title 23, CCR (DWR)
Tier 4.relationship: Regulatory linkage to rates-of-decline justification becomes especially salient
Tier 4.note: Minimum thresholds for chronic lowering supported by "the rate of groundwater elevation decline..."

Tier 4.policy_name: DWR Review/Evaluation Standard for GSPs — Water Code § 10733.4
Tier 4.relationship: State oversight more likely to be implicated
Tier 4.note: DWR evaluation/assessment authority (risk of "deficiencies" and "corrective actions").

Tier 4.policy_name: State Intervention / Probationary Basin Standard — Water Code § 10735.2 (State Water Board)
Tier 4.relationship: State oversight more likely to be implicated
Tier 4.note: If DWR determines a plan is inadequate or not implemented to likely achieve sustainability, State Water Board intervention becomes possible: SWRCB factsheet: "DWR... determines a plan is not being implemented... likely to achieve sustainability..." Statute: SWRCB may designate a basin probationary.

Tier 4.policy_name: Well Construction Standards & Local Permitting — Water Code §§ 13800 et seq.
Tier 4.relationship: Ancillary regulatory implications (common in Tier 4 conditions)
Tier 4.note: Well permitting pressure/deeper wells -> county LEA well-permitting regimes become operationally stressed/active.

Tier 4.policy_name: Porter–Cologne Water Quality Control Act — Water Code Division 7
Tier 4.relationship: Ancillary regulatory implications (common in Tier 4 conditions)
Tier 4.note: If "storage recovery" is pursued through recharge projects, water-quality permits/conditions under Porter-Cologne may be implicated.

Governing Agencies.name: Local Groundwater Sustainability Agencies (GSAs)
Governing Agencies.note: Set basin sustainability goals; adopt/enforce pumping/recharge management to avoid 'undesirable results' (including storage loss). Authority derives from SGMA definitions/requirements.

Governing Agencies.name: California Department of Water Resources (DWR)
Governing Agencies.note: Defines basin framework (Bulletin 118); evaluates GSPs and plan implementation likelihood of meeting sustainability.

Governing Agencies.name: State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB)
Governing Agencies.note: SGMA state intervention (probationary basins/interim plans) when statutory triggers are met.

Governing Agencies.name: Regional Water Quality Control Boards (RWQCBs) + SWRCB
Governing Agencies.note: Regulate discharges that may affect groundwater quality (often relevant for recharge-as-storage strategies).

Governing Agencies.name: County/Local Well Permitting Agencies (LEAs)
Governing Agencies.note: Permit wells and enforce local well standards—often stressed/implicated under declining-storage scenarios.

Governing Agencies.name: SWRCB – Division of Drinking Water (DDW)
Governing Agencies.note: Additional requirements for wells supplying public water systems (often implicated when falling storage/levels affect supply reliability).
